question.text: A Cat II AIF's Manager is structuring an SPV in Mauritius to route investment into a UK portfolio company. Tax counsel warns that the Indian tax authorities can invoke GAAR. Which of the following is the CORRECT description of when GAAR applies?

answer.text: GAAR applies to every cross-border transaction by default.

GAAR applies when the main purpose of the arrangement is to obtain a tax benefit AND one of four 'tainted elements' is satisfied (non-arm's-length, misuse/abuse, lack of commercial substance, abnormal manner).
GAAR applies only when the tax benefit exceeds INR 30 crore per taxpayer per year.
GAAR only applies to foreign portfolio investors, not Indian AIFs.

explanation.text: The Logic: GAAR (Sec 95-102 ITA, effective 1 April 2017) can be invoked where an arrangement is an 'impermissible avoidance arrangement' — the main purpose is a tax benefit AND ANY ONE of four tainted elements is present: (a) rights/obligations not at arm's-length; (b) direct/indirect misuse or abuse of the ITA; (c) lack of commercial substance; (d) manner not normally employed for bona fide purposes. CBDT clarified that the INR 30 million threshold is PER arrangement, not per taxpayer, and that LOB in a treaty adequately addressing avoidance prevents GAAR invocation. The Trap: Option A over-extends GAAR to all cross-border deals (commercial substance is a defence). Option C misstates the threshold (30 million — INR 3 crore — not 30 crore) and the taxpayer-level basis. Option D wrongly confines GAAR to FPIs — it applies to any taxpayer including AIFs and their SPVs. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same GAAR framework. X-B (IA L2) uses it for advising HNIs on offshore structures. XXIV (AML) has a related anti-abuse lens but distinct from GAAR. MLI's PPT is an OVERLAY on GAAR for treaty-based planning. Manager's Pro-Tip: For every offshore SPV in your Cat II fund's structure, prepare a contemporaneous GAAR defence file: board minutes showing genuine decision-making in the SPV jurisdiction, employee/substance evidence, commercial rationale beyond tax. 'Tax treaty shopping' remains the single biggest GAAR trigger post-FY 2017-18.
